content.title: About
content.content: Pasteles are a traditional Puerto Rican dish consisting of a seasoned dough made from grated green plantain or yucca, filled with pork, olives, capers, and spices, then wrapped in banana leaves and boiled. They are especially popular during the holiday season, such as Christmas and New Year's.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pasteles are often compared to Mexican tamales, but the dough is made from yucca rather than corn masa.
The preparation is a communal activity called a "pastelada," where families and neighbors gather to make large batches together.
Banana leaves impart a distinctive aroma and keep the dough from drying out during cooking.
Traditional recipes use pork lard, though modern versions may use chicken, beef, or even seafood.
Pasteles are commonly served with tomato sauce and mustard.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Yucca provides starch that offers sustained energy and helps keep you feeling full.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat filling supplies complete protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pasteles contain vitamin B6 and niacin, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They provide potassium, magnesium, and iron, important for heart health and blood formation.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Grated yucca and added vegetables add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because pasteles are cooked with fat and meat, portion size should be moderate, especially for weight management.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Olives, capers, and sauces can raise sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some variations include shrimp or fish, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Raw yucca toxicity
items.content: Uncooked yucca contains cyanogenic glycosides and must be grated and boiled thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pasteles are usually served hot, sliced into wedges. They can be enjoyed on their own or alongside rice, beans, and a fresh salad. Many people drizzle them with tomato sauce or a mustard‑based sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pasteles in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them—first cut into portions, wrap tightly in plastic film, and place in a freezer bag.
